findings.reason: without extending `as_dict()` or excluding `admission_findings` from the equality case, the worker either fails its own first case or silently delivers a rebuild that still loses one of the five fields the section was written to recover.
findings.text: §36 says `TaskNode` "already serialises all of them (reckon/crew/node.py near line 822)", but `as_dict()` (node.py:810-836) serialises `images`, `inputs`, `compares_with` and `over_fence_reason` and does NOT serialise `admission_findings` (nor `peer_scopes`); the queued pointer is built as `"node": node.as_dict()` (dispatch.py:243), so a field `_node_from_pointer` reads from the pointer can never be present for `admission_findings`, and the done-when's first case ("equals the dispatched node in every TaskNode field") cannot hold for a node that carried them unless `as_dict()` is also extended — which is outside the section's declared write paths (queue_admission.py and the new test only)

findings.reason: adding `s36` to §14's declared waits is what makes the queue hold the drain until the launch path it exercises is repaired.
findings.text: §14's `plan-section-depends-on` entry lists §6, §13, §15 and §18–§34 but not `s36`, while §14's first sentence (plan.html:104) says the drain begins "Once every other section has landed" and §36 rewrites `_node_from_pointer`, the function every queued launch goes through (§14's own drain), so the queue may dispatch the whole-plan drain before §36 has landed
